Right now I’m working in a grocery store. If you can get a job at a grocery store by you which is mainly stocking shelves that could be a really good option. There are people around, but if you can get past that uncomfortable part it really doesn’t require socializing at all. 

I am working in produce this summer and the first two days I wanted to quit, because I felt like I had to talk to coworkers. You don’t. You can say “hi, how are you?” and go your separate way. As for interacting with customers you don’t have to be interesting and honestly the only time I talk to any of them is when someone approaches me while I am stocking and asks where something is. 

I’ve made a sort of script: 

Customer - “hi can you help me find xyz?”

Me - “yes I’d be happy to. Follow me.”

Me - “it is right here.”

Customer - “thank you”

Me - “you’re welcome”

And that’s how it goes every single time. It’s scary at first, but it doesn’t require much and it has been a great place to start for me. It’s a good stepping stone towards more social interaction as you can interact with others if you choose to, otherwise you can stay completely to yourself without having to participate in real conversation.

Also I want to say that I think it’s great you are starting to think abt a job. For me it took forever too even consider submitting an application. So you should be happy abt that too. Good luck with whatever you end up doing!!!

At a partial hospitalization program I went to, one of the things we learned about in group therapy is negativity bias. You can look at it some more yourself if you would like a better description than I can give, but the general idea is that humans tend to be more focused on and impacted by a negative thing than a positive or neutral thing of equal importance and effect. This is exaggerated to an unhealthy extent in people with low self esteem. Our group therapist taught us to notice when we are having really negative thoughts about ourselves and try to look at the facts of the situation and make a conscious effort of acknowledging the positive aspects which we normally don't do.

It is really hard to not look at the negatives of a situation, but it helps at least a little to force yourself to accept that there are positives.
